limitations: Clock-independence is proven by simulation, not by moving this machine's clock: I stamp backup_restore_barriers.restored_at to the simulated instant, which is precisely the value the production helper writes via domain.Now() at that clock, then exercise the real trigger through the real domain API. I never set or attempted to set the system clock, and I did not patch tests/domain/check/main.go (all mutation tests ran on throwaway copies outside the tracked tree).

The residual machine-time assumption is a clock-jump, not a calendar: W0301-FRESH-OBSERVATION-UNLOCKS needs the wall clock not to step backwards by more than an hour between the helper's stamp and line 353, and STALE-OBSERV-DOES-NOT-UNLOCK needs no forward jump of more than 48 hours inside the same run. Both margins are enormous for a 1.2-second run; I did not test with an injected NTP step.

Freshness is decided by lexicographic comparison of RFC3339Nano strings (shared with the legacy Run fence, pre-existing project convention): RFC3339Nano strips trailing zeros, so two instants inside the same second can order counterfactually ('...:00Z' > '...:00.5Z'). With offsets of exactly +/-1h and 48h from the barrier stamp this cannot bite - the date/time fields differ before any fraction is reached - but a durable fix should move to julianday()/unix-epoch comparison. Not new debt from this round.

My round-3 probe asserts the trigger's live behaviour through raw UPDATEs plus domain.MapClientSession/HandoffEpoch, exactly as the shipped checker does; it does not exercise Service.ObserveRuntime end-to-end (needs auth principals and a live service), same limitation as prior rounds.

Nothing in the round-3 diff (a check program and receipts) can affect them, and the fence/migration/product code is byte-identical to what I verified in round 2 (7 of 7 round-2 code hashes still match their 3225a31f blobs and the files are unchanged in the tree).

My three dispatcher invocations created execution/invocations/<uuid> directories (untracked tool data, same as every prior round) and my scratch is deleted; the only new file I wrote into the tracked namespace is this JSON.
